title: Normalized reduced base change over a complete trait
statement: Let $D$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction field $F$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be flat, separated and of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There is a finite field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], with no separability requirement, for which the following holds. Write $V\subset L$ for the integral closure of $D$ in $L$ (the elements satisfying monic polynomials over $D$) [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $V$ is a complete discrete valuation ring, has fraction field $L$, is finite as a $D$-module, and $D\hookrightarrow V$ is local, meaning that the maximal ideal of $V$ contracts to that of $D$. Put $X_V=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}D}\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-pc-base-change], let $H=(X_V)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and let $\nu:N\to H$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. The schemes $H$ and $N$ are flat, separated and of finite type over $V$, and $\nu$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The generic fibre $H_L$ is geometrically reduced, the generic fibre $N_L$ is geometrically normal, and the closed fibre $N_{V/\mathfrak m_V}$ is geometrically reduced. Here geometrically reduced means reduced after every extension of the indicated field; geometrically normal means that after every such extension all local rings are integrally closed domains. Reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent local sections. No affineness, reducedness, irreducibility, or generic smoothness of $X$ is assumed; the empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/qrg.pdf, Appendix by Brian Conrad, Theorem A.2 and Remark A.3, printed p.28; compare Stacks Tag 09IL (more-morphisms.tex, theorem-normalized-base-change-with-reduced-fibre), whose Nagata hypothesis holds for a complete DVR.

proof.text: We first record the construction over any complete DVR $W$ arising as the integral closure of $D$ in a finite extension $K/F$. The complete-DVR normalization theorem gives all assertions about $W$, including finiteness, locality and fraction field $K$. Base change preserves flatness, separatedness and finite type of $X_W$. On a finite affine cover write $X_W=\bigcup\operatorname{Spec}T_a$; the $T_a$ are finite type and flat over $W$. They are Noetherian since a DVR is a Noetherian PID. For a uniformizer $\rho$ and $\rho t$ nilpotent in $T_a$, one has $\rho^nt^n=0$ for some $n$, so flatness gives $t^n=0$. Thus $A_a=(T_a)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is torsion free over $W$, hence flat. Its quotient presentation is finite type. The reduction immersion is finite, so $H_W=(X_W)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is separated and finite type over $W$. This applies also to $W=D$.

source.place: Setup before Tag 09IL; reduction flatness also Conrad Appendix opening paragraph, printed p.28.

proof.text: For this $W$, completeness implies that $W$ is Nagata and hence universally Japanese. On each chart $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ of $H_W$, the affine normalization formula gives $\nu^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A_a)=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$, with $B_a=\prod_j\overline{A_a/\mathfrak p_j}$, where $\mathfrak p_j$ runs through the finitely many minimal primes and the bars mean integral closure in the respective fraction fields. Each $A_a/\mathfrak p_j$ is a finite type domain over $W$, so universal Japaneseness says its closure in its own fraction field is finite. Consequently the finite product $B_a$ is finite over $A_a$. This proves finiteness of the componentwise normalization $N_W\to H_W$. It is surjective and normal by the normalization-properties node. Since a finite morphism over a separated finite-type scheme has separated finite-type source, $N_W$ has both properties over $W$.

source.place: Setup before Tag 09IL; Algebra Tags 032W, 0334; Morphisms Tags 035P and 0CDV.

proof.text: The uniformizer $\rho$ is a nonzerodivisor on each $A_a$. The product-of-fields formula for $Q(A_a)$ shows that $\rho$ remains a nonzerodivisor in $B_a\subset Q(A_a)$: it is nonzero in every minimal-prime field. Thus $B_a$ is torsion free, hence flat over the PID $W$. Normalization is therefore $W$-flat. Reduction and normalization commute with inverting $\rho$. For reduction, if $t/\rho^m$ is nilpotent then $\rho^rt^n=0$ for some $r,n$, and $(\rho^rt)^n=0$, so it already lies in the localized nilradical; the converse is immediate. For normalization apply integral-closure localization to $A_a\subset Q(A_a)$; inverting the nonzerodivisor $\rho$ does not change the total fraction ring. Therefore $(H_W)_K=(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $(N_W)_K$ is its componentwise normalization. These identifications agree on overlaps by the restriction clause of normalization. All the preceding constructions allow zero rings, empty schemes and empty closed fibres.

source.place: Setup and normalized base-change diagram preceding Tag 09IL; Algebra Tag 0307; Morphisms Tags 035P, 035K.

proof.text: The finite type generic fibre $X_F$ has finitely many irreducible components: take its finite affine cover, use finite type Noetherianity and finite minimal primes on each chart. Apply finite inseparable geometric reduction to obtain $F_1/F$ for which $Z=(X_{F_1})_{\mathrm{red}}$ is geometrically reduced. Apply the geometrically-normal-normalization preparation node to $Z/F_1$, obtaining $K/F_1$ finite purely inseparable such that its normalization after base change to $K$ is geometrically normal. Here $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}=Z_K$: the nilradical ideal of the Noetherian scheme $X_{F_1}$ is nilpotent; after base change its quotient $Z_K$ is reduced by geometric reducedness, so this ideal is exactly the new nilradical. Let $W_0$ be the integral closure of $D$ in $K$, and put $H_0=(X_{W_0})_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $N_0=H_0^\nu$. Steps 1–3 give finite flat separated finite-type models, with $(H_0)_K$ geometrically reduced and $(N_0)_K$ geometrically normal. The new field-extension normalization lemma, applied to every affine chart of $(H_0)_K$, shows that for every further field extension $M/K$, $(N_0)_M$ is the normalization of $(H_0)_M$ and is geometrically normal. The generic-fibre identifications are the actual normalization maps, not merely abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09IL first paragraph, with Varieties Tags 04KT and 0BXT to prepare both generic-fibre clauses; persistence uses Tag 0C3N.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $N_0=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}E_i$. Each $E_i$ is a finite type flat $W_0$-algebra with geometrically normal generic fibre. The affine Raynaud–Faltings node therefore supplies a finite extension $K_i/K$ for each $i$. Write $W_i$ for the integral closure of $W_0$ in $K_i$, and $C_i$ for the integral closure of $E_i\otimes_{W_0}W_i$ in $E_i\otimes_{W_0}K_i$. The cited node gives that $C_i$ is finite, normal and flat, has that very generic fibre, and has geometrically reduced special fibre. The complete-DVR normalization theorem makes every $W_i$ a finite complete DVR over $W_0$. Choose a common finite complete DVR extension $V/W_0$ receiving local maps from all $W_i$, using the common-extension node; if the cover is empty take $V=W_0$. Put $L=\operatorname{Frac}V$. Products of finite spanning sets show $L/F$ is finite. The uniqueness clause for integral closures of complete DVRs identifies $V$ with the integral closure of $D$ in $L$, and gives all its asserted completeness, finiteness and locality properties.

source.place: Tag 09IL finite common extension; Conrad Appendix A.2 locally on the total space. Affine input read with its geometric-normal-generic-fibre hypothesis.

proof.text: For each $i$ set $P_i=C_i\otimes_{W_i}V$ and $A_i=E_i\otimes_{W_0}V$. The ring $P_i$ is a finite $A_i$-module by tensoring a finite set of module generators. It is $V$-flat by flat base change, and its generic fibre is $E_i\otimes_{W_0}L$, normal by Step 4. Its special fibre is $(C_i/\mathfrak m_{W_i}C_i)\otimes_{k_i}k_V$: the local map sends $\mathfrak m_{W_i}$ into $\mathfrak m_V$, so this identity follows directly from tensoring with $k_V$. It is geometrically reduced, including after any extension of $k_V$, by the affine node's conclusion. Apply the normal-generic/reduced-special DVR criterion to $P_i$ to conclude it is normal. Flatness embeds $P_i$ into its generic fibre, and hence embeds $A_i$ there too. The normal-total-fractions node implies that $P_i$ is exactly the integral closure of $A_i$ inside $E_i\otimes_{W_0}L$: it is integral over $A_i$ because it is finite; conversely an element of this generic ring integral over $A_i$ is integral over $P_i$ and belongs to $P_i$, since the generic ring is its localization at the uniformizer. The ring $A_i$ is Noetherian and, as a subring of the normal, hence reduced, ring $E_i\otimes_{W_0}L=A_i[1/\pi]$, reduced; so $(N_0)_V$ is reduced and Noetherian, as the affine normalization formula requires. Since $\pi$ is a nonzerodivisor on $A_i$, an element $a/\pi^n$ is a nonzerodivisor of $A_i[1/\pi]$ exactly when $a$ is one of $A_i$, so $Q(A_i)=Q(A_i[1/\pi])$. By the normal-total-fractions node the normal ring $A_i[1/\pi]$ is integrally closed in this common total fraction ring, so every element of $Q(A_i)$ integral over $A_i$ lies in $E_i\otimes_{W_0}L$, hence in $P_i$. Thus, by the affine normalization formula, normalization of $(N_0)_V$ has, on this cover, the charts $\operatorname{Spec}P_i$. In particular its closed fibre is geometrically reduced.

source.place: Conrad Appendix Remark A.3, persistence under further Dedekind extensions; affine normality supplied by the existing DVR criterion. Tensor and monic-polynomial argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Finally put $H=(X_V)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $N=H^\nu$ as in the statement. The flat scheme $(H_0)_V$ has reduced generic fibre $(H_0)_L$, so it is reduced: a nilpotent section maps to zero generically and is killed by a power of the uniformizer, and torsion freeness makes it zero. The nilpotent ideal of $H_0\hookrightarrow X_{W_0}$ remains nilpotent after base change, so $(H_0)_V=H$. Normalization of $(N_0)_V$ is canonically $N$. To check this without assuming normalization commutes with arbitrary trait base change, work on any affine chart of $H_0$, with normalization rings $A\subset B$. After tensoring with $V$ these still inject into their generic fibres. By Step 4 the map $B_L\to A_L$ on spectra is the normalization map, so $A_L$ and $B_L$ have the same total fraction ring. Inverting the uniformizer shows $Q(A_V)=Q(B_V)$ as well. The algebra $B_V$ is finite and hence integral over $A_V$. In the common total fraction ring, their integral closures agree: integrality over $B_V$ implies integrality over $A_V$ by transitivity, and the reverse inclusion follows by using the same monic polynomial. The affine normalization formula and restriction compatibility identify the two global normalizations. Step 6 now gives the geometrically reduced closed fibre of $N$. Steps 1–3 give finite surjectivity of $\nu$, flatness, separatedness and finite type of $H,N$; Step 4 gives their required generic-fibre properties after $K\subset L$. This proves every clause, including $X=\varnothing$.
